restatements.text: Lowers the state minimum wage to $15.00 per hour beginning January 1, 2028.

evidence.quote: the state minimum wage is $15.00 per hour.
evidence.why: The text lowers the required minimum wage from $17.00 to $15.00 per hour, which decreases a direct labor cost for businesses.

evidence.why: The text lowers the state minimum wage from the current $17.00 per hour to $15.00 per hour, reducing minimum pay.

analysis.answer: Current law sets the state minimum wage at $17.00 per hour. This measure lowers the state minimum wage to $15.00 per hour, effective January 1, 2028.
Direct labor costs for employers of low-wage workers will decrease. Workers who currently earn between $15.00 and $17.00 per hour will face lower required minimum earnings.
Workers making between $15.00 and $17.00 per hour bear the cost of lower mandated wages. Businesses that employ minimum-wage workers benefit from reduced labor costs.

Employers might hire more workers, offer more hours, or lower the prices of their goods and services due to reduced labor costs. Workers might seek more hours, look for higher-paying jobs, or leave the labor force.

The measure addresses the high cost of labor for businesses and potential barriers to entry-level hiring by lowering the legal wage floor. It may create challenges for low-wage workers trying to meet living expenses on a lower minimum wage.
Employers gain more discretion over wage setting for jobs previously mandated to pay between $15.00 and $17.00 per hour.

The effect of minimum wage levels on employment is heavily disputed. Some researchers find that lowering the minimum wage increases hiring and reduces prices, while others find that wage floors have little to no negative effect on employment and primarily serve to boost worker incomes.
No significant change in administration or enforcement is expected, as the measure simply changes the rate of an existing rule.
The measure is a statutory change to the minimum wage and could be undone by future legislation.

flags.note: The measure specifies an effective date of January 1, 2028.
